The test image shows a field-level view with rows of soybean plants. Some plants appear yellowed/lighter among predominantly green plants, with yellow research flags marking affected areas. This patchy, field-wide chlorosis/yellowing pattern suggests a systemic or soil-borne disease. Top candidates: Sudden_death_syndrome, Soybean_Cyst_Nematode, Phytophthora, Brown_Stem_Rot.

Let me view reference images one at a time across candidates.
SDS reference shows close-up interveinal necrosis — quite different from the field-level view in the test image. Let me check Soybean_Cyst_Nematode which often shows field-level patchy symptoms.
This SCN reference shows field-level yellowing canopy — closer to the test image scale. Let me check another SCN reference and Phytophthora.
SCN root image — doesn't match test image. Let me check Phytophthora for field-level symptoms.
Let me check Brown_Stem_Rot and the third SCN reference for comparison.

This SCN reference (Soybean_Dise_32) shows field-level rows with yellowing plants on the left vs. healthy green on the right — very similar to the test image pattern. Let me check two more candidates.
SDS field view shows a distant wide-angle shot with a pale patch — less similar to the test image's close-up row view. Let me check Green_stem_disorder.
I need to check one more class. Let me view Brown_Stem_Rot.

Brown_Stem_Rot shows a split stem with internal browning — clearly a close-up diagnostic image, not matching the test image's field-level view.

**Summary of evidence:**
- Test image: field-level rows of soybeans with patchy yellowing/chlorosis among green plants, yellow research flags marking affected spots
- SCN_32 reference matched most closely: field rows with yellowing plants on one side vs. healthy green on the other — same scale, same pattern
- SCN_27 also showed field-level canopy yellowing at similar scale
- All other references (SDS, Phytophthora, BSR, Green_stem_disorder) showed close-up symptoms not matching the field-level patchy pattern

The patchy field-level yellowing across rows is the classic aboveground symptom of Soybean Cyst Nematode, and the SCN reference images matched the test image most directly in terms of visual appearance, scale, and pattern.
